vars.label: Expected annual loss from natural hazards, $ a year
vars.ref: FEMA National Risk Index (December 2025), expected annual loss
vars.definition: FEMA's estimate of the average loss each year, in dollars, to buildings, agriculture and lives (lives valued in dollars by FEMA's rule), from the 18 hazards of the National Risk Index. Puerto Rico's value is the sum of the municipios. A model estimate, not a record of losses.

vars.label: Expected annual loss from hurricane (wind), $ a year
vars.ref: FEMA National Risk Index (December 2025), expected annual loss
vars.definition: FEMA's estimate of the average loss each year, in dollars, to buildings, agriculture and lives (lives valued in dollars by FEMA's rule), from hurricane (wind) alone. Blank where FEMA does not model the hazard for the municipio. A model estimate, not a record of losses.

Blank where FEMA does not model the hazard for the municipio. A model estimate, not a record of losses.

vars.label: Landslides mapped after Hurricane María (2017)
vars.ref: USGS slope-failure locations after Hurricane María (Hughes and others, 2019)
vars.definition: Slope failures (landslides, debris flows and rock falls) that USGS and UPRM geologists mapped from aerial images taken after Hurricane María, by the municipal boundary that holds each one's point. It shows where the 2017 rains set off slides, a record of one storm, not a forecast.

vars.label: Landslides mapped after Hurricane María, per km² of land
vars.ref: USGS slope-failure locations after Hurricane María (Hughes and others, 2019)
vars.definition: The same slope failures divided by the municipio's land area in square kilometres (Census).

vars.label: Wetlands, km²
vars.definition: The area of the wetlands the National Wetlands Inventory maps in the municipio, almost all of it from aerial photographs of 1983 (estuarine and marine wetlands, among them mangroves, beaches and tidal flats; freshwater marshes; freshwater swamps and shrub wetlands), in square kilometres. Lakes, ponds, rivers and open water are left out. A wetland across a boundary is split; the part beyond the drawn coast goes to the municipio with the largest share.

vars.label: Wetlands, % of land area
vars.definition: Wetland area divided by the municipio's land area (Census), in percent. Coastal wetlands can lie partly on what the Census counts as water.

vars.label: Mangroves, km²
vars.definition: The area of the inventory's estuarine intertidal forested and scrub-shrub wetlands with broad-leaved evergreen plants (codes E2FO3 and E2SS3), which in Puerto Rico are mangroves, in square kilometres, as mapped from photographs of 1983.

fema_nri.name: FEMA — National Risk Index, county table
fema_nri.note: Expected annual loss for each municipality, in all and by hazard. FEMA leaves the composite risk score, social vulnerability and community resilience empty for Puerto Rico.

usgs_slope_failures.name: USGS — Map of slope-failure locations in Puerto Rico after Hurricane María (Hughes and others, 2019)
usgs_slope_failures.note: Read from the copy the data release's first author keeps at the University of Puerto Rico at Mayagüez (the USGS catalogue refuses scripts). Counted by point in the municipal boundary.

usfws_nwi.name: US Fish and Wildlife Service — National Wetlands Inventory
usfws_nwi.note: Wetland polygons of Puerto Rico from the inventory's map service, split among the municipal boundaries.

nri.note: FEMA leaves the composite risk score, social vulnerability and community resilience empty for Puerto Rico; the Community Resilience Estimates (hazard_series.json) fill part of the gap.

wetlands.mapped_from: colour-infrared aerial photographs of February 1983 for the coasts (about a third of the island, holding almost all of the wetland area); most of the interior is the inventory's interim scalable product, and a few small areas come from later photographs
